findings.text: Forward bounded search over a cursor prepares lock state, attempts an initial setup step, and when setup indicates continuation delegates remaining work to forward slot advance in range mode, with retry responsibility for stale nodes left to that advance step.

Reverse search variants share a common reverse setup phase before delegating to reverse slot advance; one requests single entry stepping while the other requests range stepping, and both leave stale node retries to the advance step.

Reverse setup normalizes cursor position relative to a lower bound across distinct cursor phases. Error completes immediately, active proceeds to bound validation, start triggers an initial walk, pause and none adjust stored position before restarting, overflow and underflow reinterpret stored position as past or before current location, and root proceeds. After setup, pointer cursors resolve to absent, empty walks reset to root with zeroed position and expose the root, otherwise the cursor is ready for reverse stepping only when still at or above the bound.

Erase at the current cursor position ensures walkability, locates the present value, and when present resets the cursor, reserves write resources, retries through a must succeed allocation path on pressure, applies a null store, releases temporary resources, and returns the prior value; absent locations skip the store and still release resources.

Erase and must succeed allocation interact with tree locking. Erase hints at possible allocation when an external lock is in use. The must succeed helper requires the tree lock on entry, reports no work when the cursor is not in an out of memory error, otherwise obtains nodes in a mode that cannot fail, temporarily releasing and reacquiring only the internal lock when no external lock protects the tree, then restores the requested interval and reports that the caller must retry.

Boot initialization establishes the dedicated node cache for fixed size tree nodes, aligned to the node size, with a modest per sheaf reserve, using a name identifying maple nodes and a policy that panics if creation fails.

Point lookup under read side protection starts a cursor over a single key, treats absent and pointer only states as misses with special handling that preserves the zero key case, walks toward the entry, retries when still in the initial phase without a value, normalizes zero coded values to null, and always exits the read side section before returning.
Single key store is a thin delegation to a range store over an interval where both ends equal the target key.
Single key insertion delegates to range insertion over a degenerate interval.

Range insertion rejects advanced coded values and inverted intervals with an invalid argument result, otherwise attempts insertion under exclusive protection, repeating the attempt while allocation pressure is reported, then translates any cursor error into a numeric status and releases temporary resources.

Mutating range operations serialize with an exclusive tree lock held across search plus insert or erase work, releasing before translating errors and destroying cursor state. Duplication with locking nests the destination outer and the source inner with a single depth nesting annotation.

Forward allocation finds a free interval of a requested size within caller bounds on trees marked allocatable, rejects reserved coded values, inserts the supplied value at the located start, and reports that start on success. Reverse allocation follows the same contract using reverse empty search. Cyclic allocation validates the same preconditions then delegates interval choice to a cyclic helper that advances a caller supplied cursor.

Allocation search plus insert is not atomic under memory pressure because the pressure helper may release the exclusive lock; the implementation therefore repeats empty area search after such a release to avoid using a stale location, and only reports the stored start when no cursor error remains.
Single key erase traces the operation, hints at possible allocation, performs the erase under exclusive protection, and returns the removed value.

Tree duplication requires identical attributes between source and destination and an empty destination, otherwise records an invalid argument error. Pointer only and empty sources share flags and height and publish the source root directly. Other trees allocate a fresh root, copy nodes depth first left to right, allocating children only for branches, stepping across leaves until the maximum key, then repair the root parent, synchronize flags, publish the new root with release semantics, and discard spare nodes.

Node copy for duplication replicates the full node storage then rewires the parent link to a supplied new parent while preserving type mask bits from the prior parent encoding. Child allocation for branches counts occupied positions, requests that many nodes, propagates allocation errors, and populates new slots with fresh nodes combined with preserved type bits from locked source slots without publishing them for concurrent readers yet.

Partial duplicates on out of memory are reclaimed by walking toward the root and bulk freeing child groups after clearing node mask bits, then freeing the root allocation; the walk is skipped when no node was ever established. Both duplication wrappers only invoke this reclamation for out of memory failures and otherwise propagate the mapped error code.

Unlocked duplication builds directly and maps cursor errors to a return code, leaving locking to the caller. Locked duplication acquires the destination then the source with nesting, builds, releases the source, maps errors and conditionally reclaims, then releases the destination.

Ordered search from a caller index up to a maximum rejects inverted starts, walks under read side protection with a retry while still initial, normalizes zero coded values to null, scans forward while active and before the maximum when no value was found, and on success advances the caller index to one past the located end.
Search after a position rejects a zero start as a miss and otherwise delegates to ordered search, so callers must present a nonzero resume key.
Two atomic counters record how many self test runs started and how many passed.

Cache tuning helpers forward a caller value to the node cache for non kernel marking, callback installation, private data installation, allocation size query, and allocation count query or reset. Allocation count wrappers report current totals while the reset wrapper clears the tracked total.
Cache shrink has two build dependent forms sharing one name: one is a no operation and the other forwards to the cache shrink operation.

Node access uses type specific slot tables selected by the encoded node type, with slot retrieval through an offset helper, pivot arrays for range limits, gap arrays for free space accounting on capable types, and parent links that combine a pointer with low mask bits preserved across duplication and cleared before bulk free.

Diagnostic dump of a whole tree reports identity, flags, height and root, then dispatches on root kind to node, single entry, or empty rendering. Node rendering indents by depth, prints ranges in hexadecimal or decimal, distinguishes dense leaf, range, and allocation range layouts, decodes value, zero, reserved and pointer entries distinctly, iterates slots deriving per slot intervals from pivots, recursing into children or entries, and reports an error when a derived interval extends beyond the supplied maximum.

Dump traversal stops at empty trailing slots, skips zero length pivots beyond the first position, and treats reaching the maximum as completion, otherwise advancing the next start to one past the current end.

Depth first postorder stepping bounded by a maximum attempts a forward node move and returns early unless overflow occurred; for non root overflow it ascends once then rewinds fully before restoring the saved parent position, so callers must not assume cursor offsets survive this repositioning.

Gap validation recomputes the largest free extent per visited node. Dense nodes count the longest run of empty slots. Other layouts compare stored gaps against pivot derived spans and track the maximum. Allocation range nodes additionally verify that the recorded largest gap index is in range and points at the computed maximum and that gaps beyond the occupied limit are zero. Non root nodes verify that the parent gap entry for the current slot equals the recomputed maximum. The routed excerpt ends mid check, so remaining assertions are not visible.

Maximum key uses the largest unsigned long value to denote full range coverage and duplication completion; zero coded entries are externally normalized to null; inverted intervals, non allocatable trees for allocation, mismatched duplication attributes, and non empty duplication destinations all map to invalid argument; allocation exhaustion maps to out of memory.

Must succeed allocation combines the normal kernel allocation mode with a no fail modifier; duplication locking uses a single depth nesting level; node cache creation aligns to node size with a per sheaf reserve of thirty two and a panic policy on failure.
